52	---
53	# Workflow: context read/write
54	
55	## When to use
56	Whenever a role is about to act on, or record into, the shared verified context. Every role reads the verified context before it works and records its results after it verifies them. This workflow is the single source of the context read/write protocol: read-before-act, do the work, write-after-verify. It also holds the admission rules that decide what may enter the verified context. Every other workflow and role references this file rather than restating the protocol — there is one protocol, named here, not forked into each role.
57	
58	The only sanctioned writer of the shared context is `scripts/context-io.ts` (compiled to `scripts/context-io.js`). No role and no workflow writes the `.grugops/context/` path by any other path. The note schema this workflow records into is `agent-factory/contracts/context-note.md`.
59	
60	## Agents involved
61	- Every role. This workflow is a seam, not an SDLC stage: it has no owning specialist and no queue of its own. Whichever role is about to act on, or record into, the shared verified context runs this protocol, then returns to the workflow it came from.
62	- The §14 gate (`agent-factory/workflows/05-pr-quality-gate.md`) is the only issuer of a `§14-gate#<id>` verification stamp, and a named human is the only issuer of `human:<name>`. Neither is a participant here; both are the authorities admission checks against.
63	
64	## Inputs required
65	- The task id whose shared context is being read or written.
66	- The existing verified context for that task, read through `context-io.ts` (`readContext` / `render`) — the prior findings, decisions and recorded dead ends.
67	- The note schema `agent-factory/contracts/context-note.md` — the shape a note must take to be admissible.
68	- A real verification stamp for a `finding`, and for no other kind: a live green `§14-gate#<id>` verdict, or `human:<name>` under a named human's session grant.
69	- The `human_admission` dial from the target repository's factory configuration, on EVERY host. Which repository that is comes from the resolution order `context-io.ts` publishes and step 3 below states; it is not a Claude-Code-only read.
70	
71	## Steps
72	Run these in order. The order is the protocol — read the verified state first, work, then record only what verification admits.
73	
74	1. Read the shared context for the task through `context-io.ts` (`readContext` / `render`) before doing the work. Start from the verified state, not a blank slate. The prior verified findings, decisions, and recorded failed attempts are the memory you build on. Do not re-derive what the context already holds. Do not retry a recorded failed attempt.
75	
76	2. Implement the change, run the analysis, or make the decision the task needs.
77	
78	3. Record notes ONLY through the sanctioned writer — never author the context path by hand. A note written by any other route (a file-writing tool, a heredoc, an editor) is refused on read as `unsealed`. On Claude Code the sanctioned admission path for a verified note is the STRUCTURED tool `mcp__plugin_grugops_grugops__propose_note`. The scoped name is the platform's name for the plugin's bundled server; `mcp__grugops__propose_note` is the server's own name. The agent admits a note by structured JSON arguments, not a shell command string. There is no command text to obfuscate. That tool routes its persistence through `context-io.ts` (`admitAndAppend` → `appendNote`) internally. So `context-io.ts` remains the single sanctioned writer of the shared context — "record only via context-io" still holds. Choose the note kind honestly:
79	   - Record a `finding` (a verified result) ONLY with a real verification stamp in `verified_by`. The two accepted stamps are `§14-gate#<id>` and `human:<name>`. Cross-check `§14-gate#<id>` against a live GREEN gate verdict (Posture B). The `<id>` matches a live green `§14-gate` verdict record under the task. Use `human:<name>` for non-gate-adjudicable judgment or an unsolvable disagreement only (the escalation valve). On Claude Code the separate PER-CALL PreToolUse `admission-guard` hook makes the `human:<name>` signal un-forgeable. That hook gates the `mcp__plugin_grugops_grugops__propose_note` channel and the bare `mcp__grugops__` spelling. It is a distinct process that reads the FRESH session variable per call. The agent's own child env cannot reach that variable. It validates the agent-supplied `human:<name>` stamp against the variable on every call. It reads the FINAL structured tool arguments, not a Bash command string. The grant is session-scoped and per-note capable (D-07). Once a named human exports `GRUGOPS_ADMISSION_APPROVED_BY=<name>`, it authorizes high-severity admissions under that name for the rest of the session. The human controls granularity by setting/unsetting the grant around a specific disposition. The per-call hook re-reads the fresh env, so an unset takes effect on the next call. The grant is not a mechanically-enforced per-note nonce. The Claude Code primary tier is gated by the `human_admission` dial. The four non-CC CLIs degrade to two weaker signals. They get the in-script `admit()` refusal plus a prompt-level "stop, ask a named human" (D-04/D-05). `appendNote`, the writer Workflow 17 prescribes, reaches that refusal for every note it takes rather than for one kind. That refusal is decided against the TARGET repository's dial, under a resolution order `context-io.ts` states in one place. The first step is `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` when it names something. The second is the installer-set `GRUGOPS_PROJECT_DIR`. The third is the repository root's own configuration where the upward search reaches a repository root. Otherwise it is the nearest ancestor carrying a factory configuration. The last is the shared kit. The upward search is bounded above, and every condition that stops it is stated once in the section below. `GRUGOPS_PROJECT_DIR` is the documented non-Claude-Code answer and the installer sets it, not the agent. Where no step names a configured repository the dial read is the shared kit's shipped lean default. The lean default is the correct answer for a repository that configured nothing. That degradation is documented honestly as not mechanically un-forgeable. The GOV-02 ledger's `disposed_by: human:<name>` means "admitted under <name>'s session grant," not "individually reviewed each entry."
80	   - Record a soft or neutral result as a `claim` or an `observation`, which needs no stamp. Only a `finding` requires `verified_by`. The `claim` / `decision` / `failed-attempt` / `observation` / `artifact-ref` kinds are soft, neutral, or pointer by nature.
81	   - Identify the gate's own green verdict as the one allowed `by: §14-gate` self-attestation. The §14 gate emits it only on a green result (see `agent-factory/workflows/05-pr-quality-gate.md`), the root of the verification chain. Any other note authored `by: §14-gate` is a structural FAIL (an auditable impersonation flag).
82	
83	4. Read the admission refusal, then take ONE of the two honest routes below. `context-io.ts` hard-rejects a stampless or invalid-stamp `finding` — it names the fault and refuses the write. It NEVER silently rewrites the note into a `claim` (silent mutation is a fabrication smell).
84	   - Obtain a real stamp within budget. Run or fix the §14 gate to earn the real `§14-gate#<id>` stamp. Work inside the EXISTING bounded `self_fix_attempts` loop in `agent-factory/workflows/05-pr-quality-gate.md` (default `2`, "two rounds then human"). That loop lives there — this workflow references it and does not restate or re-dial it. After the budget is spent, stop and hand to a human.
85	   - Degrade honestly to a `claim`. Record the result as a `claim` carrying `confidence: UNKNOWN - verify` — explicitly non-load-bearing. A `claim` NEVER satisfies a finding's admission requirement. The gate holds the same "advise loudly, never hide" floor: never a faked pass, never a hand-set green.
86	
87	The three admission outcomes, stated once:
88	- Run the §14 gate when the result is **gate-verifiable** → green verdict → `finding` with `§14-gate#<id>` admitted. The workhorse path; no human is bothered.
89	- Record an honest `claim` with `confidence: UNKNOWN - verify` when the result is **not gate-verifiable and low-stakes**. The escape hatch; no human is bothered.
90	- Escalate to a named human → `human:<name>` when the result is **not gate-verifiable and high-stakes**, or when agents disagree. The rare path.
91	
92	## Stop conditions
93	- A `finding`'s admission is refused, and the bounded `self_fix_attempts` budget is exhausted without a real stamp → stop and hand to a human. The budget is referenced from `05-pr-quality-gate.md`. Do not loop, do not fake a stamp. `checkpoint: exhaust_self_fix_budget`
94	- The result is high-stakes and not gate-adjudicable, or agents disagree and cannot resolve it → escalate to a named human (`human:<name>`); do not self-stamp. `checkpoint: escalate_unadjudicable_result`
95	- The only way to record the result would be to hand-write the `.grugops/context/` path → stop; the sanctioned writer is `context-io.ts`.
96	
97	## The governance-root resolution order
98	
99	Every tier of the resolution order is quoted from `TRUSTED_ROOT_TIERS` in `scripts/context-io.ts`. `scripts/context-io.test.ts` asserts this list equal to that export in both directions. Every tier the program publishes appears here. Every numbered tier line here is one the program has. Neither side can move without the other. A sixth tier cannot arrive in prose alone. A program tier cannot arrive undocumented.
100	
101	0. **Tier 0** — the root the HOST delivered. It is read from `GRUGOPS_HOST_DELIVERED_ROOT` on the decider's own spawn environment. It is accepted only when it canonicalises to an existing directory. That directory carries a version-control marker. It is not the kit's own root. Otherwise this tier answers nothing and the next one runs. This tier exists on the **Claude Code hook path only**. That host builds the environment of the hook subprocess it spawns. `hooks/hook-entry.js` is byte-frozen and hash-verifies the decider before it runs. Those two facts are what make the channel one the agent cannot write. The name is not what makes it one. Its value on that path is derived from `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, which is the tier 1 ambient name. The wrapper reads that value, checks its shape and promotes it under the tier 0 name. Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and Copilot CLI deliver nothing here. The tiers below are their answer.
102	1. **Tier 1** — `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` when present and non-empty after trimming, made absolute and canonicalised through the one ladder.
103	2. **Tier 2** — `GRUGOPS_PROJECT_DIR`, the documented installer-set variable, under the same predicate.
104	3. **Tier 3** — the configuration that governs the process working directory. It is the repository root's own where the upward search reaches a boundary carrying one. Otherwise it is the nearest ancestor carrying a factory configuration. It is bounded above as the section below states.
105	4. **Tier 4** — the shared kit this reader ships in, whose shipped dial is the lean default.
106	
107	**What tier 0 does not establish.** It closes the tier that decides whether a force push runs. It closes nothing about a process acting as itself. An agent can invoke `scripts/context-io.js` directly from its own Bash tool. That agent builds its own environment and can set that name. It is an already-accepted capability, recorded as `R-31-15-01`. Members of `TRUSTED_ROOT_RESIDUALS` that tier 0 closes here carry `hosts: non-cc-hook-path`. They remain open on the four hosts where no such channel exists. Members that stand everywhere carry `hosts: all`.
108	
109	## Where the upward governance-root search stops
110	
111	Every stop condition of step 3's upward search, quoted from `TRUSTED_ROOT_STOP_CONDITIONS` in `scripts/context-io.ts`. `scripts/context-io.test.ts` asserts this list equal to that export in both directions. Neither can move without the other. The bound is the home-directory stop. It bounds ascent, not observation. The home directory itself is read once and answers only as a repository. It holds whatever markers a filesystem carries. The version-control markers say where a repository starts, which is a different question.
112	
113	- The upward search never inspects any ancestor of the user's home directory.
114	- The user's home directory itself is inspected exactly once and ends the upward search either way. It is adopted only when it carries a version-control marker and its configuration sits at the repository state-plane position rather than the in-kit position. That candidate must also not be one of the running kit's own fallback candidate positions.
115	- When the home directory cannot be determined, the upward search does not run at all.
116	- The upward search ends at the first ancestor carrying a version-control marker.
117	- That ancestor's own configuration outranks one nested below it.
118	- The upward search ends at the filesystem root.
119	- The upward search inspects at most 64 ancestors.
120	
121	## Board moves
122	None of its own. This workflow is a seam every role passes through, not a column of work — running it never moves a ticket on `plans/board.md`. The board move belongs to the workflow that invoked it (04, 05, 14, 15 and the rest). That workflow makes the move on its own terms. A read or a write here neither advances nor holds a ticket.
123	
124	## Trace updates
125	None of its own. The requirement→code→test→release trail in `plans/traceability.md` is rendered from the admitted notes. So this workflow feeds the trace rather than editing it: an `artifact-ref` note carries the trace ids, and the render picks them up. The invoking workflow appends and updates its own rows. Never hand-edit a traceability row to stand in for a note that admission refused — that is a faked trace.
126	
127	## Done condition
128	The task's verified context was read before work began. Every result was recorded via `context-io.ts` under the honest kind. A `finding` carries a real `§14-gate#<id>` or `human:<name>` stamp that admission accepts; soft results are recorded as `claim` / `observation`. No refused finding was faked into a pass or silently degraded. Any refusal was resolved by earning a real stamp within budget, or by honest re-record as a `claim` with `confidence: UNKNOWN - verify`.
129	
130	## Commit
131	Commit the context notes this workflow wrote per `agent-factory/_commit-convention.md` — branch guard first (never a protected branch), then `type(scope): summary`. The artifacts are the `notes/` files and the derived `index.md` / `index.jsonl` renders that `context-io.ts` produced. This workflow records verified context; it never merges and never deploys — humans hold both.
132	---
133	kind: workflow
134	order: 17
135	cadence: both
136	---
137	# Workflow: task claim + schedule
138	
139	## When to use
140	Whenever a role is about to take ownership of a queued subtask, or the coordinator is about to schedule the queue. This workflow is the single source of the claim+schedule protocol. The protocol covers how a pending subtask is claimed exactly once and how it transitions pending → claimed → done. It also covers how a stale claim is reclaimed. Every role references this file rather than restating — there is one protocol, named here, not forked into each role.
141	
142	It builds directly on `agent-factory/workflows/16-context-read-write.md` (the read/write/admission protocol) for all note I/O and does not restate it. The claim layer owns work-ownership; WF16 owns what enters the shared verified context.
143	
144	## Agents involved
145	- Every role that takes a queued subtask. Like Workflow 16 this is a seam, not an SDLC stage: it has no owning specialist. Whichever role is about to take ownership runs this protocol, then returns to the workflow it came from.
146	- The coordinator, in one extra capacity only: it schedules the queue and runs the wall-clock stale-claim sweep. It does not claim on another role's behalf and it does not adjudicate a lost claim.
147	
148	## Inputs required
149	- The queue root and the subtask id under `pending/`.
150	- The subtask's existing shared verified context, read per Workflow 16 before the claim.
151	- `queue.stale_ttl_minutes` from `.grugops/factory.config.json` — the TTL the coordinator's sweep derives `ttlMs` from.
152	- The claiming identity (`by`) written into the now-running registry record.
153	
154	## The claim/note seam
155	Two distinct things, never blurred:
156	
157	- **The queue CLAIM** — hard work-ownership via an atomic directory create (`scripts/claim.js` `claimTask`). The claim directory's existence IS the claim; there is no central lock manager. The claim is the concurrency net under the substrate: a task is claimed exactly once, so within-task context writing is single-writer.
158	- **The `claim` note-KIND** (WF16 / `context-io.ts`) — a soft, unverified assertion in the shared context. It is unrelated to the queue claim and shares no code path. The now-running registry record (`claimed/<task>/claim.md`) is NOT a `kind: claim` note.
159	
160	The queue owns ownership; WF16 owns memory. Never write the shared context by claiming, and never claim by writing a note.
161	
162	## Steps
163	Run these in order.
164	
165	1. Read the subtask's shared context per WF16 (`readContext` / `render`) before claiming. Start from the verified findings, decisions, and recorded failed attempts, not a blank slate. Do not re-derive what the context already holds; do not retry a recorded failed attempt.
166	
167	2. Claim a pending subtask atomically via `scripts/claim.js` `claimTask(queueRoot, task, by)`. The first claimant's atomic `mkdirSync` of `claimed/<task>/` wins and returns true. It writes the now-running registry record `claimed/<task>/claim.md` (`by` / `at` / `task`). A second claimant gets `EEXIST` = claim lost, and returns false — NOT an error. ANY other code (parent-missing, permission) is a genuine failure and is rethrown. If the claim is lost, move to the next pending task — never two agents on one task.
168	
169	3. Transition the subtask file `pending/<task>.md` → `claimed/<task>/<task>.md` by `claim.js` `transition` (atomic rename). The claim directory already exists, because step 2 created it.
170	
171	4. Implement the subtask. Write only after you verify. Record results into the shared verified context ONLY via WF16 (`context-io.ts` `appendNote`) under the honest note kind. A `finding` needs a real stamp; soft results go in as `claim` / `observation`. Evidence pointing at a committed UAT spec goes in as an `artifact-ref`. It carries `sha`, `gate_run` and `content_hash`. `appendNote` consults the admission authority for EVERY note it takes, whatever its kind. A `finding` stamped `§14-gate#<id>` is admitted only against a live green verdict with that per-run id. An `artifact-ref` is admitted only against a live green verdict for its `gate_run`. Anything the authority refuses is refused here, and nothing is written. The admission rules live in WF16; this workflow references them and does not restate them. Coordination is ONLY through the on-disk substrate — never relay data agent-to-agent.
172	
173	5. Mark the subtask done. Transition `claimed/<task>/<task>.md` → `done/<task>.md` by `claim.js` `transition` (atomic rename) once the work is recorded and verified.
174	
175	6. Run the coordinator's stale-claim sweep periodically — `claim.js` `sweepStale(queueRoot, ttlMs)`, with `ttlMs` derived from `queue.stale_ttl_minutes`. A claim whose `claim.md` `at` is older than the TTL is reclaimed, and so is a tampered multi-`at` record. The subtask returns to `pending/` (atomic rename) and the claim directory is released. Wall-clock TTL only; no pid/host liveness. A fresh claim is left untouched (the sweep is conservative and has a real no-op path).
176	
177	## Stop conditions
178	- The claim is lost (`claimTask` returns false / `EEXIST`) → do not proceed on that task; move to the next pending task. Do not retry the same claim in a tight loop.
179	- `claimTask` throws any code other than `EEXIST` (parent missing, permission) → stop; a real error is never swallowed into a false "lost". Surface it.
180	- A result cannot be honestly admitted by WF16 (no real stamp, budget exhausted) → stop and hand to a human per WF16. Do not fake a stamp; do not mark the task done on an unverified result. `checkpoint: exhaust_self_fix_budget`
181	
182	## Board moves
183	None of its own. The queue and `plans/board.md` are two different substrates and must never be conflated. The queue tracks subtask ownership (pending → claimed → done) inside one ticket's work, while the board tracks the ticket through the delivery columns. Claiming a subtask does not move a ticket, and moving a ticket does not claim anything. The board move belongs to the invoking workflow.
184	
185	## Trace updates
186	None of its own. Ownership is not part of the requirement→code→test→release trail — `plans/traceability.md` records what was built and verified, not who picked it up. The now-running registry record (`claimed/<task>/claim.md`) is the ownership record and is complete on its own. Any trace row this subtask's results deserve is appended by the invoking workflow from the notes admitted per Workflow 16.
187	
188	## Done condition
189	The subtask was claimed exactly once (atomic `mkdirSync`), and transitioned pending → claimed → done by atomic rename. Its results were recorded only through WF16 (`context-io.ts`) under an honest kind. No data was relayed agent-to-agent — coordination flowed only through the on-disk queue and shared context. Any stale or tampered claim was reclaimed by the coordinator's wall-clock sweep.
190	
191	## Commit
192	Commit the queue and context state this workflow advanced per `agent-factory/_commit-convention.md` — branch guard first (never a protected branch), then `type(scope): summary`. The artifacts are the moved subtask records and any `notes/` / derived `index.*` that `context-io.ts` produced. This workflow claims and schedules work; it never merges and never deploys — humans hold both.
193	---
194	kind: contract
195	contract: context-note-schema
196	requirement: SCTX-01
197	---
198	
199	# Contract: the shared-context note schema (SCTX-01)
200	
201	This document is the authoritative schema for a **context note** — the typed,
202	provenance-stamped unit of the shared verified context. Every note that an agent records is
203	one of these. The schema is written in clear professional voice because it is a trace and
204	safety surface: the notes are the auditable record on which later work is built, and the
205	validator that admits or rejects a note enforces exactly the rules stated here.
206	
207	The only sanctioned writer of context notes is `scripts/context-io.ts` (compiled to
208	`scripts/context-io.js`). Roles and workflows never write the shared context by any other
209	path. This document defines the format that `context-io.ts` composes and validates against.
210	
211	## Storage model
212	
213	A note is a single markdown file: **YAML frontmatter followed by a markdown body**. Every
214	role, workflow, and skill file already uses the same CommonMark + frontmatter shape.
215	
216	Notes live under a per-task folder:
217	
218	```
219	.grugops/context/<task>/
220	  notes/        append-only raw note files — the source of truth, git-tracked, RETAINED
221	  index.md      DERIVED, human-facing consolidated render (deterministic, zero-token)
222	  index.jsonl   DERIVED, machine-parsable event index (one line per note)
223	```
224	
225	The markdown files under `notes/` are the **source of truth**. `index.md` and `index.jsonl`
226	are derived, byte-reproducible renders of the `notes/` frontmatter. Neither carries any
227	information that is not already in `notes/`. On any conflict, the markdown notes win and the
228	files are regenerated from them.
229	
230	A note file is **append-only**: recording a note writes one new file. An existing note file
231	is never mutated or deleted. Correcting or replacing an earlier note is done by writing a new
232	note whose `supersedes` field names the earlier note's id (see below) — the earlier file
233	stays in `notes/` as part of the permanent audit trail.
234	
235	## Note identity
236	
237	A note's id and filename are:
238	
239	```
240	<at-compact>-<by>-<kind>-<nonce>.md
241	```
242	
243	for example `20260617T142305Z-engineer-finding-a1b2.md`, where:
244	
245	- `<at-compact>` is the note's `at` timestamp with separators stripped (a legible `ls`
246	  timeline);
247	- `<by>` is the authoring role or agent;
248	- `<kind>` is the note kind (one of the six values below);
249	- `<nonce>` is a short slice of `crypto.randomUUID()` (from `node:crypto`).
250	
251	The `<nonce>` is a **collision-avoidance nonce, not a security token**. Its only job is to
252	keep two writers that record a note in the same millisecond from choosing the same filename
253	and clobbering each other. No secrecy, unforgeability, or authentication property is claimed
254	of it; it must never be treated as a credential or capability token.
255	
256	The filename is for storage and legibility only. **The authoritative order of the trace is
257	the `at` and `supersedes` fields, never the filename, never `ls`/`readdir` order, and never
258	file modification time.** Replay (reconstructing current state) sorts by `at` (ISO-8601
259	lexicographic) with the note id as a deterministic tiebreak, then folds out any note named in
260	a later note's `supersedes`. See SCTX-04.
261	
262	## The provenance fence (frontmatter keys)
263	
264	Every note's frontmatter carries these provenance keys:
265	
266	| Key           | Type                       | Meaning |
267	| ------------- | -------------------------- | ------- |
268	| `id`          | string                     | The note's stable creation-time identity (`<at-compact>-<by>-<kind>-<nonce>`), frozen at write and equal to the `<id>.md` filename. Carried verbatim through compaction — a load-bearing field the carve-out matches raw→promoted on and byte-equal-checks. |
269	| `kind`        | one of the six values      | What kind of note this is. |
270	| `by`          | string                     | The authoring role or agent. |
271	| `at`          | ISO-8601 timestamp string  | When the note was recorded. The authoritative replay sort key. |
272	| `verified_by` | string (may be empty)      | What verified this note's claim. For a `finding` it must carry a real `§14-gate#<id>` stamp (gate-verified) or a `human:<name>` stamp (escalation); other kinds may leave it empty. |
273	| `confidence`  | string                     | The author's confidence (e.g. `high` / `medium` / `low` / `UNKNOWN - verify`). |
274	| `refs`        | YAML list (may be empty)   | References this note points at — requirement ids, file paths, ticket refs. The trace-migration substrate (SCTX-04). |
275	| `supersedes`  | note-id ref, or empty      | The id of an earlier note this one overrides. Empty when the note supersedes nothing. |
276	| `seal`        | `sha256:` + 64 lowercase hex | Written only by the sanctioned writer (`scripts/context-io.ts`, `composeNote`), never by hand. A sha256 digest over the note's bytes without this line, always the LAST line inside the fence. A note whose seal is absent, malformed, or mismatched is returned by no reader. Every reader route refuses it: `readContext`, `render`, `currentState`, the compactor's promoted-tier carve-out, and every consumer of `readContext`. The reader counts it under the `unsealed` skip arm with the reason word (`absent`, `malformed`, `mismatch`). |
277	
278	Two note shapes carry further keys beyond this table: an `artifact-ref` that points at a committed
279	UAT spec, and the `§14-gate` verdict. Both are described under *Evidence provenance* below.
280	
281	### The seal, and what it does and does not distinguish
282	
283	The seal exists because the round-1 live capture of Phase 33 showed nine notes written into
284	`.grugops/context/<task>/notes/` with a file-writing tool, and the reader admitted every one: nothing
285	in the bytes told a note the writer composed from a note a hand composed. The seal is that
286	distinction, made mechanical. The writer emits it in one place; the reader verifies it through one
287	exported predicate (`sealVerdict`); the compactor imports that predicate rather than computing a
288	digest of its own. There is no grandfather clause: a note composed by a kit version that predates
289	the seal is refused on read like any other unsealed note, because an age exemption is exactly the
290	arm a hand-writer would take. Such a store is re-admitted through the writer, not read as it stands.
291	
292	The seal is **unkeyed**, and it is unkeyed by necessity: a file-based kit holds no secret that the
293	process it constrains cannot also read, so a keyed digest would be a key stored beside the lock.
294	What the seal therefore distinguishes is a note composed by the sanctioned writer from a note
295	composed by hand, and it detects any edit made after the write. What it does **not** do is stop a
296	process that reimplements the algorithm and writes a sealed note directly; that process is one
297	register over, not blocked. The tier that would make a hand-written note unforgeable is a
298	point-of-effect deny of file-writing tools under the context root. That tier is a kit capability
299	decision left to a human and not taken in Phase 33.
300	
301	The four required fields below are the **validator's** rule and are unchanged by the seal; the seal
302	is a **reader's** rule, asked after a note parses and before it is returned.
303	
304	### Required-field rule (the validator contract)
305	
306	A note is **structurally valid** only if all four of these required fields are present:
307	
308	- `kind`
309	- `by`
310	- `at`
311	- `confidence`
312	
313	A note missing any one of them is a **structural FAIL**. The validator names the missing
314	field; it never silently accepts an incomplete note. The required-field rule is the
315	no-fabrication floor: an unstamped note cannot enter the verified context.
316	
317	`supersedes` and `refs` **may be empty** on any note. `verified_by` **may be empty** only on a
318	soft or neutral kind (`claim` / `decision` / `failed-attempt` / `observation` / `artifact-ref`);
319	on a `finding` it is enforced. The admission rules that give `verified_by` teeth are now live in
320	`scripts/context-io.ts`: a `finding` is admitted only with a real verification stamp, and an
321	agent's self-set stamp is refused. Specifically, for a `finding` the validator is a structural
322	FAIL when `verified_by` is empty, is a literal `self` / `me` / `agent`, equals the note's own
323	`by` (self-stamp), is a DeLM invalid-evidence phrase, or matches neither accepted grammar — the
324	refuse-self FAIL set. A `verified_by: §14-gate#<id>` stamp additionally cross-checks a live GREEN
325	gate verdict carrying that per-run id (Posture B): a stamp that matches no live green verdict is
326	refused. A `human:<name>` stamp is accepted structurally; on Claude Code its un-forgeable human-set
327	signal is delivered by the separate PER-CALL PreToolUse `admission-guard` hook that gates the
328	STRUCTURED `mcp__plugin_grugops_grugops__propose_note` admission channel (the platform's scoped name
329	for the plugin's bundled server; the bare `mcp__grugops__propose_note` is the server's own name, and
330	the hook's matcher covers both spellings) — a distinct process that reads the FRESH
331	session variable per call (the variable the agent's own child env cannot reach) and validates the
332	agent-supplied `human:<name>` stamp against it on every call (mirroring the prod-deploy guard). The
333	hook reads the FINAL structured tool arguments, not a Bash command string, so there is no command
334	text to obfuscate. The grant is session-scoped and per-note capable (D-07): once a named human
335	exports the approval variable, it authorizes high-severity admissions under that name for the rest of
336	the session, and the human controls granularity by setting/unsetting the grant around a specific
337	disposition (the per-call hook re-reads the fresh env, so an unset takes effect on the next call); it
338	is not a mechanically-enforced per-note nonce. The GOV-02 ledger's `disposed_by: human:<name>`
339	therefore means "admitted under <name>'s session grant," not "individually reviewed each entry." The structured channel routes its persistence through `context-io.ts`
340	(`admitAndAppend` → `appendNote`), so `context-io.ts` remains the single sanctioned writer. That hook
341	is the Claude Code primary tier, gated by the `human_admission` dial; the four non-CC CLIs degrade to
342	the in-script `admit()` refusal plus a prompt-level "stop, ask a named human," documented honestly as
343	not mechanically un-forgeable (D-04/D-05). The reserved `by: §14-gate` identity is itself
344	a structural FAIL on any note except the gate's own verdict emission — the one root-of-trust carve-out.
345	
346	## The six note kinds
347	
348	`kind` is exactly one of these six values. A `kind` outside this set is a structural FAIL
349	that names the offending value.
350	
351	| Kind             | What it records |
352	| ---------------- | --------------- |
353	| `claim`          | A soft, unverified assertion the author believes but has not proven. |
354	| `finding`        | A verified result — something established by evidence (e.g. a passing gate). |
355	| `decision`       | A choice made, with its rationale, that constrains later work. |
356	| `failed-attempt` | An approach that was tried and did not work, recorded so it is not retried. |
357	| `observation`    | A neutral fact noticed during the work, not asserted as a claim or proven as a finding. |
358	| `artifact-ref`   | A pointer to a produced artifact (a file, a PR, a report) by reference. When it points at a committed UAT spec it also carries the evidence-provenance keys described in the next section. |
359	
360	## Evidence provenance
361	
362	An `artifact-ref` that points at a committed UAT spec carries three further frontmatter keys. They
363	exist so a piece of evidence can be bound to the commit the §14 quality gate re-ran it at.
364	
365	| Key            | Type                 | Meaning |
366	| -------------- | -------------------- | ------- |
367	| `sha`          | lowercase hex string | The commit the referenced spec was run at. |
368	| `gate_run`     | per-run id string    | The `<id>` of the `§14-gate` verdict that certifies that run. |
369	| `content_hash` | sha256 hex digest    | sha256 over the bytes of the committed `*.uat.spec.ts` file at `sha`. |
370	
371	All three are **required and non-empty on an `artifact-ref`**, and **absent on every other kind**.
372	`sha` and `content_hash` are held to an anchored lowercase-hex allowlist (`^[0-9a-f]{7,64}$`);
373	`gate_run` is a per-run id rather than a digest, so it is held to the single-line field rule and
374	nothing further. A note that breaks any of these rules is a structural FAIL that names the field.
375	
376	There is one exception, and it is narrow. The `§14-gate` verdict note records `sha` — the commit
377	its own run was performed at — and carries neither `gate_run` nor `content_hash`, because the
378	verdict *is* the run and it references no artifact. That recorded value is what an `artifact-ref`'s
379	`sha` is compared against: `admit()` refuses an `artifact-ref` whose `sha` differs from the SHA
380	recorded by the live green verdict its `gate_run` names, and it names both SHAs in the refusal. An
381	`artifact-ref` naming a `gate_run` with no live green verdict, or one whose verdict recorded no SHA
382	at all, is refused for the same reason — evidence that cannot be bound to a run is not evidence.
383	The comparison is made in `admit()` at write time and nowhere else, so there is one implementation
384	of that rule rather than two that can come to disagree.
385	
386	**The six-kind schema stays closed.** No evidence kind is added. Evidence is recorded as a
387	`finding` stamped `verified_by: §14-gate#<id>` paired with an `artifact-ref` carrying the three keys
388	above — both of them existing kinds, validated and admitted by the rules already stated here.
389	
390	**What `content_hash` is, and what it is not.** It is a recomputable integrity digest: anyone with
391	the repository can run sha256 over the spec file at `sha` and compare the result. It is **not a
392	security token and it is not tamper-proof**. No secrecy, unforgeability, or authentication property
393	is claimed of it; it must never be treated as a credential or capability token. A writer able to
394	change the note is equally able to change the digest inside it. What the digest is worth is that a
395	reader can tell whether the file at `sha` is the file the note describes.
396	
397	**Disclosed limit: transitive imports are not hashed.** `content_hash` covers the bytes of the
398	`*.uat.spec.ts` file and nothing that file imports. An edit to a helper the spec imports therefore
399	leaves the digest unchanged and leaves the evidence standing. The narrow file-only coverage is the
400	stated scope of the digest, not an oversight; a reader who needs the helper covered checks it
401	separately.
402	
403	## CRITICAL DISTINCTION: the `claim` note-KIND is NOT the queue CLAIM
404	
405	The `claim` note-KIND and the queue CLAIM are two unrelated concepts that happen to share the word
406	"claim". They must never be blurred in a single sentence, a shared field, or a shared code path.
407	
408	**The `claim` note-KIND** is one of the six `kind:` values above. It is a soft, unverified
409	assertion recorded as a note file under `.grugops/context/<task>/notes/`. It carries no
410	ownership and grants no exclusivity. It lives entirely inside the shared-context substrate.
411	
412	**The queue CLAIM** is hard work-ownership. An agent claims a task by atomically creating the
413	directory `.grugops/queue/claimed/<task>/` (via `mkdirSync`) and writing a `claim.md` record
414	inside it (CLAIM-01 / CLAIM-02, delivered in plan 20-02). A second agent's `mkdir` on the
415	same path throws `EEXIST`, which is the unambiguous "claim lost" signal. The queue CLAIM is a
416	filesystem ownership primitive; it is not a note and has no `kind`.
417	
418	A `claim`-kind note is an *assertion in the context*; a queue CLAIM is *ownership of work in
419	the queue*. They are different mechanisms with different files, different directories, and
420	different purposes.
421	
422	**The `claim`-kind cannot satisfy a finding's admission (now enforced, VFY-04):** a `claim`-kind
423	note can never, on its own, satisfy a `finding`'s admission requirement. A claim is soft until
424	something verifies it; only a verified result is a `finding`. `scripts/context-io.ts` enforces
425	this: a `finding` is admitted only with a real verification stamp, so a claim cannot masquerade
426	as a verified finding. When a finding's stamp is refused, the agent honestly re-records the
427	result as a `claim` with `confidence: UNKNOWN - verify` — it never fakes a pass.
428	
429	## Worked example: a valid note
430	
431	```markdown
432	---
433	id: 20260617T142305Z-software-engineer-finding-a1b2
434	kind: finding
435	by: software-engineer
436	at: 2026-06-17T14:23:05Z
437	verified_by: §14-gate#ABC-001
438	confidence: high
439	refs:
440	  - AUTH-01
441	  - src/api/auth.ts
442	supersedes: 
443	---
444	
445	The login endpoint rejects an expired token with a 401 and an audit log line.
446	Verified by the §14 quality gate run ABC-001 (lint + tests + UI/E2E all green).
447	```
448	
449	This note is structurally valid: `kind`, `by`, `at`, and `confidence` are all present and
450	`kind` is one of the six values. `id` is the note's frozen creation-time identity and equals
451	the `<id>.md` filename. `verified_by` carries a gate stamp, `refs` is a YAML list, and
452	`supersedes` is empty (this note overrides nothing).

56	# Workflow: context read/write
57	
58	## When to use
59	Whenever a role is about to act on, or record into, the shared verified context. Every role reads the verified context before it works and records its results after it verifies them. This workflow is the single source of the context read/write protocol: read-before-act, do the work, write-after-verify. It also holds the admission rules that decide what may enter the verified context. Every other workflow and role references this file rather than restating the protocol — there is one protocol, named here, not forked into each role.
60	
61	The only sanctioned writer of the shared context is `scripts/context-io.ts` (compiled to `scripts/context-io.js`). No role and no workflow writes the `.grugops/context/` path by any other path. The note schema this workflow records into is `agent-factory/contracts/context-note.md`.
62	
63	## Agents involved
64	- Every role. This workflow is a seam, not an SDLC stage: it has no owning specialist and no queue of its own. Whichever role is about to act on, or record into, the shared verified context runs this protocol, then returns to the workflow it came from.
65	- The §14 gate (`agent-factory/workflows/05-pr-quality-gate.md`) is the only issuer of a `§14-gate#<id>` verification stamp, and a named human is the only issuer of `human:<name>`. Neither is a participant here; both are the authorities admission checks against.
66	
67	## Inputs required
68	- The task id whose shared context is being read or written.
69	- The existing verified context for that task, read through `context-io.ts` (`readContext` / `render`) — the prior findings, decisions and recorded dead ends.
70	- The note schema `agent-factory/contracts/context-note.md` — the shape a note must take to be admissible.
71	- A real verification stamp for a `finding`, and for no other kind: a live green `§14-gate#<id>` verdict, or `human:<name>` under a named human's session grant.
72	- The `human_admission` dial from the target repository's factory configuration, on EVERY host. Which repository that is comes from the resolution order `context-io.ts` publishes and step 3 below states; it is not a Claude-Code-only read.
73	
74	## Steps
75	Run these in order. The order is the protocol — read the verified state first, work, then record only what verification admits.
76	
77	1. Read the shared context for the task through `context-io.ts` (`readContext` / `render`) before doing the work. Start from the verified state, not a blank slate. The prior verified findings, decisions, and recorded failed attempts are the memory you build on. Do not re-derive what the context already holds. Do not retry a recorded failed attempt.
78	
79	2. Implement the change, run the analysis, or make the decision the task needs.
80	
81	3. Record notes ONLY through the sanctioned writer — never author the context path by hand. A note written by any other route (a file-writing tool, a heredoc, an editor) is refused on read as `unsealed`. On Claude Code the sanctioned admission path for a verified note is the STRUCTURED tool `mcp__plugin_grugops_grugops__propose_note`. The scoped name is the platform's name for the plugin's bundled server; `mcp__grugops__propose_note` is the server's own name. The agent admits a note by structured JSON arguments, not a shell command string. There is no command text to obfuscate. That tool routes its persistence through `context-io.ts` (`admitAndAppend` → `appendNote`) internally. So `context-io.ts` remains the single sanctioned writer of the shared context — "record only via context-io" still holds. Choose the note kind honestly:
82	   - Record a `finding` (a verified result) ONLY with a real verification stamp in `verified_by`. The two accepted stamps are `§14-gate#<id>` and `human:<name>`. Cross-check `§14-gate#<id>` against a live GREEN gate verdict (Posture B). The `<id>` matches a live green `§14-gate` verdict record under the task. Use `human:<name>` for non-gate-adjudicable judgment or an unsolvable disagreement only (the escalation valve). On Claude Code the separate PER-CALL PreToolUse `admission-guard` hook makes the `human:<name>` signal un-forgeable. That hook gates the `mcp__plugin_grugops_grugops__propose_note` channel and the bare `mcp__grugops__` spelling. It is a distinct process that reads the FRESH session variable per call. The agent's own child env cannot reach that variable. It validates the agent-supplied `human:<name>` stamp against the variable on every call. It reads the FINAL structured tool arguments, not a Bash command string. The grant is session-scoped and per-note capable (D-07). Once a named human exports `GRUGOPS_ADMISSION_APPROVED_BY=<name>`, it authorizes high-severity admissions under that name for the rest of the session. The human controls granularity by setting/unsetting the grant around a specific disposition. The per-call hook re-reads the fresh env, so an unset takes effect on the next call. The grant is not a mechanically-enforced per-note nonce. The Claude Code primary tier is gated by the `human_admission` dial. The four non-CC CLIs degrade to two weaker signals. They get the in-script `admit()` refusal plus a prompt-level "stop, ask a named human" (D-04/D-05). `appendNote`, the writer Workflow 17 prescribes, reaches that refusal for every note it takes rather than for one kind. That refusal is decided against the TARGET repository's dial, under a resolution order `context-io.ts` states in one place. The first step is `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` when it names something. The second is the installer-set `GRUGOPS_PROJECT_DIR`. The third is the repository root's own configuration where the upward search reaches a repository root. Otherwise it is the nearest ancestor carrying a factory configuration. The last is the shared kit. The upward search is bounded above, and every condition that stops it is stated once in the section below. `GRUGOPS_PROJECT_DIR` is the documented non-Claude-Code answer and the installer sets it, not the agent. Where no step names a configured repository the dial read is the shared kit's shipped lean default. The lean default is the correct answer for a repository that configured nothing. That degradation is documented honestly as not mechanically un-forgeable. The GOV-02 ledger's `disposed_by: human:<name>` means "admitted under <name>'s session grant," not "individually reviewed each entry."
83	   - Record a soft or neutral result as a `claim` or an `observation`, which needs no stamp. Only a `finding` requires `verified_by`. The `claim` / `decision` / `failed-attempt` / `observation` / `artifact-ref` kinds are soft, neutral, or pointer by nature.
84	   - Identify the gate's own green verdict as the one allowed `by: §14-gate` self-attestation. The §14 gate emits it only on a green result (see `agent-factory/workflows/05-pr-quality-gate.md`), the root of the verification chain. Any other note authored `by: §14-gate` is a structural FAIL (an auditable impersonation flag).
85	
86	4. Read the admission refusal, then take ONE of the two honest routes below. `context-io.ts` hard-rejects a stampless or invalid-stamp `finding` — it names the fault and refuses the write. It NEVER silently rewrites the note into a `claim` (silent mutation is a fabrication smell).
87	   - Obtain a real stamp within budget. Run or fix the §14 gate to earn the real `§14-gate#<id>` stamp. Work inside the EXISTING bounded `self_fix_attempts` loop in `agent-factory/workflows/05-pr-quality-gate.md` (default `2`, "two rounds then human"). That loop lives there — this workflow references it and does not restate or re-dial it. After the budget is spent, stop and hand to a human.
88	   - Degrade honestly to a `claim`. Record the result as a `claim` carrying `confidence: UNKNOWN - verify` — explicitly non-load-bearing. A `claim` NEVER satisfies a finding's admission requirement. The gate holds the same "advise loudly, never hide" floor: never a faked pass, never a hand-set green.
89	
90	The three admission outcomes, stated once:
91	- Run the §14 gate when the result is **gate-verifiable** → green verdict → `finding` with `§14-gate#<id>` admitted. The workhorse path; no human is bothered.
92	- Record an honest `claim` with `confidence: UNKNOWN - verify` when the result is **not gate-verifiable and low-stakes**. The escape hatch; no human is bothered.
93	- Escalate to a named human → `human:<name>` when the result is **not gate-verifiable and high-stakes**, or when agents disagree. The rare path.
94	
95	## Stop conditions
96	- A `finding`'s admission is refused, and the bounded `self_fix_attempts` budget is exhausted without a real stamp → stop and hand to a human. The budget is referenced from `05-pr-quality-gate.md`. Do not loop, do not fake a stamp. `checkpoint: exhaust_self_fix_budget`
97	- The result is high-stakes and not gate-adjudicable, or agents disagree and cannot resolve it → escalate to a named human (`human:<name>`); do not self-stamp. `checkpoint: escalate_unadjudicable_result`
98	- The only way to record the result would be to hand-write the `.grugops/context/` path → stop; the sanctioned writer is `context-io.ts`.
99	
100	## The governance-root resolution order
101	
102	Every tier of the resolution order is quoted from `TRUSTED_ROOT_TIERS` in `scripts/context-io.ts`. `scripts/context-io.test.ts` asserts this list equal to that export in both directions. Every tier the program publishes appears here. Every numbered tier line here is one the program has. Neither side can move without the other. A sixth tier cannot arrive in prose alone. A program tier cannot arrive undocumented.
103	
104	0. **Tier 0** — the root the HOST delivered. It is read from `GRUGOPS_HOST_DELIVERED_ROOT` on the decider's own spawn environment. It is accepted only when it canonicalises to an existing directory. That directory carries a version-control marker. It is not the kit's own root. Otherwise this tier answers nothing and the next one runs. This tier exists on the **Claude Code hook path only**. That host builds the environment of the hook subprocess it spawns. `hooks/hook-entry.js` is byte-frozen and hash-verifies the decider before it runs. Those two facts are what make the channel one the agent cannot write. The name is not what makes it one. Its value on that path is derived from `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, which is the tier 1 ambient name. The wrapper reads that value, checks its shape and promotes it under the tier 0 name. Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and Copilot CLI deliver nothing here. The tiers below are their answer.
105	1. **Tier 1** — `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` when present and non-empty after trimming, made absolute and canonicalised through the one ladder.

140	# Workflow: task claim + schedule
141	
142	## When to use
143	Whenever a role is about to take ownership of a queued subtask, or the coordinator is about to schedule the queue. This workflow is the single source of the claim+schedule protocol. The protocol covers how a pending subtask is claimed exactly once and how it transitions pending → claimed → done. It also covers how a stale claim is reclaimed. Every role references this file rather than restating — there is one protocol, named here, not forked into each role.
144	
145	It builds directly on `agent-factory/workflows/16-context-read-write.md` (the read/write/admission protocol) for all note I/O and does not restate it. The claim layer owns work-ownership; WF16 owns what enters the shared verified context.
146	
147	## Agents involved
148	- Every role that takes a queued subtask. Like Workflow 16 this is a seam, not an SDLC stage: it has no owning specialist. Whichever role is about to take ownership runs this protocol, then returns to the workflow it came from.
149	- The coordinator, in one extra capacity only: it schedules the queue and runs the wall-clock stale-claim sweep. It does not claim on another role's behalf and it does not adjudicate a lost claim.
150	
151	## Inputs required
152	- The queue root and the subtask id under `pending/`.
153	- The subtask's existing shared verified context, read per Workflow 16 before the claim.
154	- `queue.stale_ttl_minutes` from `.grugops/factory.config.json` — the TTL the coordinator's sweep derives `ttlMs` from.
155	- The claiming identity (`by`) written into the now-running registry record.
156	
157	## The claim/note seam
158	Two distinct things, never blurred:
159	
160	- **The queue CLAIM** — hard work-ownership via an atomic directory create (`scripts/claim.js` `claimTask`). The claim directory's existence IS the claim; there is no central lock manager. The claim is the concurrency net under the substrate: a task is claimed exactly once, so within-task context writing is single-writer.
161	- **The `claim` note-KIND** (WF16 / `context-io.ts`) — a soft, unverified assertion in the shared context. It is unrelated to the queue claim and shares no code path. The now-running registry record (`claimed/<task>/claim.md`) is NOT a `kind: claim` note.
162	
163	The queue owns ownership; WF16 owns memory. Never write the shared context by claiming, and never claim by writing a note.
164	
165	## Steps
166	Run these in order.
167	
168	1. Read the subtask's shared context per WF16 (`readContext` / `render`) before claiming. Start from the verified findings, decisions, and recorded failed attempts, not a blank slate. Do not re-derive what the context already holds; do not retry a recorded failed attempt.
169	
170	2. Claim a pending subtask atomically via `scripts/claim.js` `claimTask(queueRoot, task, by)`. The first claimant's atomic `mkdirSync` of `claimed/<task>/` wins and returns true. It writes the now-running registry record `claimed/<task>/claim.md` (`by` / `at` / `task`). A second claimant gets `EEXIST` = claim lost, and returns false — NOT an error. ANY other code (parent-missing, permission) is a genuine failure and is rethrown. If the claim is lost, move to the next pending task — never two agents on one task.
171	
172	3. Transition the subtask file `pending/<task>.md` → `claimed/<task>/<task>.md` by `claim.js` `transition` (atomic rename). The claim directory already exists, because step 2 created it.
173	
174	4. Implement the subtask. Write only after you verify. Record results into the shared verified context ONLY via WF16 (`context-io.ts` `appendNote`) under the honest note kind. A `finding` needs a real stamp; soft results go in as `claim` / `observation`. Evidence pointing at a committed UAT spec goes in as an `artifact-ref`. It carries `sha`, `gate_run` and `content_hash`. `appendNote` consults the admission authority for EVERY note it takes, whatever its kind. A `finding` stamped `§14-gate#<id>` is admitted only against a live green verdict with that per-run id. An `artifact-ref` is admitted only against a live green verdict for its `gate_run`. Anything the authority refuses is refused here, and nothing is written. The admission rules live in WF16; this workflow references them and does not restate them. Coordination is ONLY through the on-disk substrate — never relay data agent-to-agent.
175	
176	5. Mark the subtask done. Transition `claimed/<task>/<task>.md` → `done/<task>.md` by `claim.js` `transition` (atomic rename) once the work is recorded and verified.
177	
178	6. Run the coordinator's stale-claim sweep periodically — `claim.js` `sweepStale(queueRoot, ttlMs)`, with `ttlMs` derived from `queue.stale_ttl_minutes`. A claim whose `claim.md` `at` is older than the TTL is reclaimed, and so is a tampered multi-`at` record. The subtask returns to `pending/` (atomic rename) and the claim directory is released. Wall-clock TTL only; no pid/host liveness. A fresh claim is left untouched (the sweep is conservative and has a real no-op path).
179	
180	## Stop conditions
181	- The claim is lost (`claimTask` returns false / `EEXIST`) → do not proceed on that task; move to the next pending task. Do not retry the same claim in a tight loop.
182	- `claimTask` throws any code other than `EEXIST` (parent missing, permission) → stop; a real error is never swallowed into a false "lost". Surface it.
183	- A result cannot be honestly admitted by WF16 (no real stamp, budget exhausted) → stop and hand to a human per WF16. Do not fake a stamp; do not mark the task done on an unverified result. `checkpoint: exhaust_self_fix_budget`
184	
185	## Board moves
186	None of its own. The queue and `plans/board.md` are two different substrates and must never be conflated. The queue tracks subtask ownership (pending → claimed → done) inside one ticket's work, while the board tracks the ticket through the delivery columns. Claiming a subtask does not move a ticket, and moving a ticket does not claim anything. The board move belongs to the invoking workflow.

189	None of its own. Ownership is not part of the requirement→code→test→release trail — `plans/traceability.md` records what was built and verified, not who picked it up. The now-running registry record (`claimed/<task>/claim.md`) is the ownership record and is complete on its own. Any trace row this subtask's results deserve is appended by the invoking workflow from the notes admitted per Workflow 16.

191	## Done condition
192	The subtask was claimed exactly once (atomic `mkdirSync`), and transitioned pending → claimed → done by atomic rename. Its results were recorded only through WF16 (`context-io.ts`) under an honest kind. No data was relayed agent-to-agent — coordination flowed only through the on-disk queue and shared context. Any stale or tampered claim was reclaimed by the coordinator's wall-clock sweep.

201	
202	# Contract: the shared-context note schema (SCTX-01)
203	
204	This document is the authoritative schema for a **context note** — the typed,
205	provenance-stamped unit of the shared verified context. Every note that an agent records is
206	one of these. The schema is written in clear professional voice because it is a trace and
207	safety surface: the notes are the auditable record on which later work is built, and the
208	validator that admits or rejects a note enforces exactly the rules stated here.
209	
210	The only sanctioned writer of context notes is `scripts/context-io.ts` (compiled to
211	`scripts/context-io.js`). Roles and workflows never write the shared context by any other
212	path. This document defines the format that `context-io.ts` composes and validates against.
213	
214	## Storage model
215	
216	A note is a single markdown file: **YAML frontmatter followed by a markdown body**. Every
217	role, workflow, and skill file already uses the same CommonMark + frontmatter shape.
218	
219	Notes live under a per-task folder:
220	
221	```
222	.grugops/context/<task>/
223	  notes/        append-only raw note files — the source of truth, git-tracked, RETAINED
224	  index.md      DERIVED, human-facing consolidated render (deterministic, zero-token)
225	  index.jsonl   DERIVED, machine-parsable event index (one line per note)
226	```
227	
228	The markdown files under `notes/` are the **source of truth**. `index.md` and `index.jsonl`
229	are derived, byte-reproducible renders of the `notes/` frontmatter. Neither carries any
230	information that is not already in `notes/`. On any conflict, the markdown notes win and the
231	files are regenerated from them.
232	
233	A note file is **append-only**: recording a note writes one new file. An existing note file
234	is never mutated or deleted. Correcting or replacing an earlier note is done by writing a new
235	note whose `supersedes` field names the earlier note's id (see below) — the earlier file
236	stays in `notes/` as part of the permanent audit trail.
237	
238	## Note identity
239	
240	A note's id and filename are:
241	
242	```
243	<at-compact>-<by>-<kind>-<nonce>.md
244	```
245	
246	for example `20260617T142305Z-engineer-finding-a1b2.md`, where:
247	
248	- `<at-compact>` is the note's `at` timestamp with separators stripped (a legible `ls`
249	  timeline);
250	- `<by>` is the authoring role or agent;
251	- `<kind>` is the note kind (one of the six values below);
252	- `<nonce>` is a short slice of `crypto.randomUUID()` (from `node:crypto`).
253	
254	The `<nonce>` is a **collision-avoidance nonce, not a security token**. Its only job is to
255	keep two writers that record a note in the same millisecond from choosing the same filename
256	and clobbering each other. No secrecy, unforgeability, or authentication property is claimed
257	of it; it must never be treated as a credential or capability token.
258	
259	The filename is for storage and legibility only. **The authoritative order of the trace is
260	the `at` and `supersedes` fields, never the filename, never `ls`/`readdir` order, and never
261	file modification time.** Replay (reconstructing current state) sorts by `at` (ISO-8601
262	lexicographic) with the note id as a deterministic tiebreak, then folds out any note named in
263	a later note's `supersedes`. See SCTX-04.
264	
265	## The provenance fence (frontmatter keys)
266	
267	Every note's frontmatter carries these provenance keys:
268	
269	| Key           | Type                       | Meaning |
270	| ------------- | -------------------------- | ------- |
271	| `id`          | string                     | The note's stable creation-time identity (`<at-compact>-<by>-<kind>-<nonce>`), frozen at write and equal to the `<id>.md` filename. Carried verbatim through compaction — a load-bearing field the carve-out matches raw→promoted on and byte-equal-checks. |
272	| `kind`        | one of the six values      | What kind of note this is. |
273	| `by`          | string                     | The authoring role or agent. |
274	| `at`          | ISO-8601 timestamp string  | When the note was recorded. The authoritative replay sort key. |
275	| `verified_by` | string (may be empty)      | What verified this note's claim. For a `finding` it must carry a real `§14-gate#<id>` stamp (gate-verified) or a `human:<name>` stamp (escalation); other kinds may leave it empty. |
276	| `confidence`  | string                     | The author's confidence (e.g. `high` / `medium` / `low` / `UNKNOWN - verify`). |
277	| `refs`        | YAML list (may be empty)   | References this note points at — requirement ids, file paths, ticket refs. The trace-migration substrate (SCTX-04). |
278	| `supersedes`  | note-id ref, or empty      | The id of an earlier note this one overrides. Empty when the note supersedes nothing. |
279	| `seal`        | `sha256:` + 64 lowercase hex | Written only by the sanctioned writer (`scripts/context-io.ts`, `composeNote`), never by hand. A sha256 digest over the note's bytes without this line, always the LAST line inside the fence. A note whose seal is absent, malformed, or mismatched is returned by no reader. Every reader route refuses it: `readContext`, `render`, `currentState`, the compactor's promoted-tier carve-out, and every consumer of `readContext`. The reader counts it under the `unsealed` skip arm with the reason word (`absent`, `malformed`, `mismatch`). |
280	
281	Two note shapes carry further keys beyond this table: an `artifact-ref` that points at a committed
282	UAT spec, and the `§14-gate` verdict. Both are described under *Evidence provenance* below.
283	
284	### The seal, and what it does and does not distinguish
285	
286	The seal exists because the round-1 live capture of Phase 33 showed nine notes written into
287	`.grugops/context/<task>/notes/` with a file-writing tool, and the reader admitted every one: nothing
288	in the bytes told a note the writer composed from a note a hand composed. The seal is that
289	distinction, made mechanical. The writer emits it in one place; the reader verifies it through one
290	exported predicate (`sealVerdict`); the compactor imports that predicate rather than computing a
291	digest of its own. There is no grandfather clause: a note composed by a kit version that predates
292	the seal is refused on read like any other unsealed note, because an age exemption is exactly the
293	arm a hand-writer would take. Such a store is re-admitted through the writer, not read as it stands.
294	
295	The seal is **unkeyed**, and it is unkeyed by necessity: a file-based kit holds no secret that the
296	process it constrains cannot also read, so a keyed digest would be a key stored beside the lock.
297	What the seal therefore distinguishes is a note composed by the sanctioned writer from a note
298	composed by hand, and it detects any edit made after the write. What it does **not** do is stop a
299	process that reimplements the algorithm and writes a sealed note directly; that process is one
300	register over, not blocked. The tier that would make a hand-written note unforgeable is a
301	point-of-effect deny of file-writing tools under the context root. That tier is a kit capability
302	decision left to a human and not taken in Phase 33.
303	
304	The four required fields below are the **validator's** rule and are unchanged by the seal; the seal
305	is a **reader's** rule, asked after a note parses and before it is returned.
306	
307	### Required-field rule (the validator contract)
308	
309	A note is **structurally valid** only if all four of these required fields are present:
310	
311	- `kind`
312	- `by`
313	- `at`
314	- `confidence`
315	
316	A note missing any one of them is a **structural FAIL**. The validator names the missing
317	field; it never silently accepts an incomplete note. The required-field rule is the
318	no-fabrication floor: an unstamped note cannot enter the verified context.
319	
320	`supersedes` and `refs` **may be empty** on any note. `verified_by` **may be empty** only on a
321	soft or neutral kind (`claim` / `decision` / `failed-attempt` / `observation` / `artifact-ref`);
322	on a `finding` it is enforced. The admission rules that give `verified_by` teeth are now live in
323	`scripts/context-io.ts`: a `finding` is admitted only with a real verification stamp, and an
324	agent's self-set stamp is refused. Specifically, for a `finding` the validator is a structural
325	FAIL when `verified_by` is empty, is a literal `self` / `me` / `agent`, equals the note's own
326	`by` (self-stamp), is a DeLM invalid-evidence phrase, or matches neither accepted grammar — the
327	refuse-self FAIL set. A `verified_by: §14-gate#<id>` stamp additionally cross-checks a live GREEN
328	gate verdict carrying that per-run id (Posture B): a stamp that matches no live green verdict is
329	refused. A `human:<name>` stamp is accepted structurally; on Claude Code its un-forgeable human-set
330	signal is delivered by the separate PER-CALL PreToolUse `admission-guard` hook that gates the
331	STRUCTURED `mcp__plugin_grugops_grugops__propose_note` admission channel (the platform's scoped name
332	for the plugin's bundled server; the bare `mcp__grugops__propose_note` is the server's own name, and
333	the hook's matcher covers both spellings) — a distinct process that reads the FRESH
334	session variable per call (the variable the agent's own child env cannot reach) and validates the
335	agent-supplied `human:<name>` stamp against it on every call (mirroring the prod-deploy guard). The
336	hook reads the FINAL structured tool arguments, not a Bash command string, so there is no command
337	text to obfuscate. The grant is session-scoped and per-note capable (D-07): once a named human
338	exports the approval variable, it authorizes high-severity admissions under that name for the rest of
339	the session, and the human controls granularity by setting/unsetting the grant around a specific
340	disposition (the per-call hook re-reads the fresh env, so an unset takes effect on the next call); it
341	is not a mechanically-enforced per-note nonce. The GOV-02 ledger's `disposed_by: human:<name>`
342	therefore means "admitted under <name>'s session grant," not "individually reviewed each entry." The structured channel routes its persistence through `context-io.ts`
343	(`admitAndAppend` → `appendNote`), so `context-io.ts` remains the single sanctioned writer. That hook
344	is the Claude Code primary tier, gated by the `human_admission` dial; the four non-CC CLIs degrade to
345	the in-script `admit()` refusal plus a prompt-level "stop, ask a named human," documented honestly as
346	not mechanically un-forgeable (D-04/D-05). The reserved `by: §14-gate` identity is itself
347	a structural FAIL on any note except the gate's own verdict emission — the one root-of-trust carve-out.
348	
349	## The six note kinds
350	
351	`kind` is exactly one of these six values. A `kind` outside this set is a structural FAIL
352	that names the offending value.
353	
354	| Kind             | What it records |
355	| ---------------- | --------------- |
356	| `claim`          | A soft, unverified assertion the author believes but has not proven. |
357	| `finding`        | A verified result — something established by evidence (e.g. a passing gate). |
358	| `decision`       | A choice made, with its rationale, that constrains later work. |
359	| `failed-attempt` | An approach that was tried and did not work, recorded so it is not retried. |
360	| `observation`    | A neutral fact noticed during the work, not asserted as a claim or proven as a finding. |
361	| `artifact-ref`   | A pointer to a produced artifact (a file, a PR, a report) by reference. When it points at a committed UAT spec it also carries the evidence-provenance keys described in the next section. |
362	
363	## Evidence provenance
364	
365	An `artifact-ref` that points at a committed UAT spec carries three further frontmatter keys. They
366	exist so a piece of evidence can be bound to the commit the §14 quality gate re-ran it at.
367	
368	| Key            | Type                 | Meaning |
369	| -------------- | -------------------- | ------- |
370	| `sha`          | lowercase hex string | The commit the referenced spec was run at. |
371	| `gate_run`     | per-run id string    | The `<id>` of the `§14-gate` verdict that certifies that run. |
372	| `content_hash` | sha256 hex digest    | sha256 over the bytes of the committed `*.uat.spec.ts` file at `sha`. |
373	
374	All three are **required and non-empty on an `artifact-ref`**, and **absent on every other kind**.
375	`sha` and `content_hash` are held to an anchored lowercase-hex allowlist (`^[0-9a-f]{7,64}$`);
376	`gate_run` is a per-run id rather than a digest, so it is held to the single-line field rule and
377	nothing further. A note that breaks any of these rules is a structural FAIL that names the field.
378	
379	There is one exception, and it is narrow. The `§14-gate` verdict note records `sha` — the commit
380	its own run was performed at — and carries neither `gate_run` nor `content_hash`, because the
381	verdict *is* the run and it references no artifact. That recorded value is what an `artifact-ref`'s
382	`sha` is compared against: `admit()` refuses an `artifact-ref` whose `sha` differs from the SHA
383	recorded by the live green verdict its `gate_run` names, and it names both SHAs in the refusal. An
384	`artifact-ref` naming a `gate_run` with no live green verdict, or one whose verdict recorded no SHA
385	at all, is refused for the same reason — evidence that cannot be bound to a run is not evidence.
386	The comparison is made in `admit()` at write time and nowhere else, so there is one implementation
387	of that rule rather than two that can come to disagree.
388	
389	**The six-kind schema stays closed.** No evidence kind is added. Evidence is recorded as a
390	`finding` stamped `verified_by: §14-gate#<id>` paired with an `artifact-ref` carrying the three keys
391	above — both of them existing kinds, validated and admitted by the rules already stated here.
392	
393	**What `content_hash` is, and what it is not.** It is a recomputable integrity digest: anyone with
394	the repository can run sha256 over the spec file at `sha` and compare the result. It is **not a
395	security token and it is not tamper-proof**. No secrecy, unforgeability, or authentication property
396	is claimed of it; it must never be treated as a credential or capability token. A writer able to
397	change the note is equally able to change the digest inside it. What the digest is worth is that a
398	reader can tell whether the file at `sha` is the file the note describes.
399	
400	**Disclosed limit: transitive imports are not hashed.** `content_hash` covers the bytes of the
401	`*.uat.spec.ts` file and nothing that file imports. An edit to a helper the spec imports therefore
402	leaves the digest unchanged and leaves the evidence standing. The narrow file-only coverage is the
403	stated scope of the digest, not an oversight; a reader who needs the helper covered checks it
404	separately.
405	
406	## CRITICAL DISTINCTION: the `claim` note-KIND is NOT the queue CLAIM
407	
408	The `claim` note-KIND and the queue CLAIM are two unrelated concepts that happen to share the word
409	"claim". They must never be blurred in a single sentence, a shared field, or a shared code path.
410	
411	**The `claim` note-KIND** is one of the six `kind:` values above. It is a soft, unverified
412	assertion recorded as a note file under `.grugops/context/<task>/notes/`. It carries no
413	ownership and grants no exclusivity. It lives entirely inside the shared-context substrate.
414	
415	**The queue CLAIM** is hard work-ownership. An agent claims a task by atomically creating the
416	directory `.grugops/queue/claimed/<task>/` (via `mkdirSync`) and writing a `claim.md` record
417	inside it (CLAIM-01 / CLAIM-02, delivered in plan 20-02). A second agent's `mkdir` on the
418	same path throws `EEXIST`, which is the unambiguous "claim lost" signal. The queue CLAIM is a
419	filesystem ownership primitive; it is not a note and has no `kind`.
420	
421	A `claim`-kind note is an *assertion in the context*; a queue CLAIM is *ownership of work in
422	the queue*. They are different mechanisms with different files, different directories, and
423	different purposes.
424	
425	**The `claim`-kind cannot satisfy a finding's admission (now enforced, VFY-04):** a `claim`-kind
426	note can never, on its own, satisfy a `finding`'s admission requirement. A claim is soft until
427	something verifies it; only a verified result is a `finding`. `scripts/context-io.ts` enforces
428	this: a `finding` is admitted only with a real verification stamp, so a claim cannot masquerade
429	as a verified finding. When a finding's stamp is refused, the agent honestly re-records the
430	result as a `claim` with `confidence: UNKNOWN - verify` — it never fakes a pass.
431	
432	## Worked example: a valid note

# Brownfield Map
_Updated: 2026-09-24 by brownfield-mapper (task `arch-audit-map`, read-only audit)_

Scope: read-only map for the request "audit current architecture". Nothing under `src/`,
`package.json`, dependencies or `AGENTS.md` was changed. Anything not run or read is marked
`UNKNOWN - verify`.

## 1. What this repo is

A tiny fixture project with the grugops factory installed on top of it. `package.json:5` says so
directly: "The runnable fixture project the Phase 33 live capture installs grugops onto". There is
one source file. Almost everything else in the tree is grugops install output (adapters, state
templates, and materialized checker tools).

- Git: branch `main`, **zero commits, zero tracked files** (`git ls-files | wc -l` = 0). Every path
  is untracked. There is no history, blame or CI record to go on.
- Runtime: Node (observed v24.12.0), ESM (`package.json:6` `"type": "module"`). No dependencies, no
  `node_modules`, no lockfile.
- Language: plain JavaScript `.mjs`. No TypeScript in the project, despite
  `.grugops/factory.config.json` `default_stack.language: "typescript"` (plus fastify, vue,
  postgresql, playwright, docker, kubernetes). **None of that stack exists in this repo.** The
  config describes intended defaults for new work, not the current system.

## 2. Structure: load-bearing vs install output vs empty

| Path | What it is | Status |
|------|------------|--------|
| `src/index.mjs` | The whole application: `greet(name)` export (`:5-7`) and a CLI mode switch on `process.argv[2]` (`:9-18`) | **Load-bearing** (the only product code) |
| `package.json` | 4 scripts, no deps | **Load-bearing** (gate commands) |
| `tools/grugops/*.js` | 3 materialized kit checkers (node builtins only) | Install output; used by the §14 gate |
| `.claude/` | 17 agent adapters, 7 skills, `settings.local.json` enables `grugops@grugops` plugin | Install output (generated, "do not hand-edit") |
| `.gemini/settings.json` | Points Gemini CLI context at `AGENTS.md` / `GEMINI.md` | Install output |
| `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | Copilot start-here pointer | Install output. **No `.github/workflows/`, so no CI** |
| `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | Agent entry docs | Install output |
| `.grugops/` | `factory.config.json`, `install.json`, `queue/` | Factory state |
| `memory-bank/` | 8 template files + ADR template | **Empty templates** (placeholders only) |
| `plans/` | board, traceability, metrics, nfr-catalog; `epics/ features/ releases/ sprints/ tickets/` hold only `.gitkeep` | **Empty templates** (no tickets, no rows) |

Nothing is dead code. The product code is small enough that there is nothing to prune.

## 3. Entrypoints

- `node src/index.mjs --self-test`: checks `greet("grug") === "hello, grug"` and prints
  `self-test: 1 case, 0 failures`. Exits 1 on mismatch (`src/index.mjs:10-15`).

  branch).
- `import { greet } from "./src/index.mjs"`: the only exported API. **Seam:** importing the module
  runs the argv switch at top level (`:9`). It is harmless today, but a side effect on import.

There is no HTTP server, no data layer and no auth. API/data/auth maps are **not applicable**.
